title: Conjunctive attribute filters — Attribute-Based Search
description: Attribute search expresses 'color=red AND year>=2020' as typed predicates over record fields. Each predicate tests one attribute; records must satisfy all of them. Conjunction over attributes is the structured counterpart of keyword AND.
demo:
# Attribute-based search: conjunctive predicates over typed record attributes.
records = [{'id': 'r1', 'color': 'red', 'year': 2021}, {'id': 'r2', 'color': 'red', 'year': 2019}, {'id': 'r3', 'color': 'blue', 'year': 2022}]
preds = [['color', '==', 'red'], ['year', '>=', 2020]]
def matches(rec):
    for attr, op, val in preds:
        v = rec.get(attr)
        if op == "==" and not (v == val): return False
        if op == ">=" and not (isinstance(v, (int, float)) and v >= val): return False
        if op == "<=" and not (isinstance(v, (int, float)) and v <= val): return False
        if op == "in" and not (v in val): return False
    return True
print("Predicates:", preds)
for r in records:
    if matches(r):
        print("MATCH:", r["id"], "-", {k: r[k] for k in r if k != "id"})
provenance: Public methodology — standard computer-science technique documented in the technical literature; fact-checked 2026-10-21.
